name: XMP Provenance Analysis
description: Analyzes XMP edit history, software chain, and provenance metadata to detect AI generation tools. Examines CreatorTool, History entries, and software agent signatures for comprehensive origin tracking.
mechanism:
The XMP provenance analysis performs deep metadata inspection:

1. **CreatorTool Analysis**: Examines the XMP CreatorTool field for AI tool signatures (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, Midjourney, ComfyUI, InvokeAI) vs legitimate photo editors (Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, Capture One, Affinity Photo).

2. **Edit History Chain**: Parses xmpMM:History entries to reconstruct the complete edit chain from creation to final save. AI-generated images typically have no history or a single 'created' action.

3. **Software Agent Fingerprinting**: Analyzes stEvt:softwareAgent entries to identify all software that touched the image. Real photos show a chain of camera firmware → RAW processor → editor.

4. **Resource Reference Tracking**: Examines xmpMM:DerivedFrom and xmpMM:DocumentID to trace image lineage — whether it's an original or derivative work.

5. **AI Marker Detection**: Searches for explicit AI generation markers that some tools embed, including custom XMP namespaces used by generative AI platforms.
parameters:
AI tool markers: Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, Midjourney, ComfyUI, InvokeAI, Leonardo.AI, Firefly, etc.
Photo editors: Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, Capture One, DxO, Affinity Photo, GIMP
XMP fields: CreatorTool, xmpMM:History, stEvt:softwareAgent, xmpMM:DerivedFrom, xmpMM:DocumentID
History actions: created, saved, converted, derived
accuracy: Very High - 90%+ when AI tool signatures are present in XMP data. Lower when XMP has been stripped.
source: Adobe XMP Specification Part 1-3 (ISO 16684), Dublin Core Metadata Initiative
useCase: Comprehensive provenance verification for images that retain XMP metadata. Essential for authenticating images in professional workflows where edit history integrity matters — journalism, stock photography, legal evidence.
strengths:
• Edit history chain provides complete image provenance
• Software agent fingerprinting reveals the full processing pipeline
• AI tool signatures in CreatorTool are highly reliable
• Resource references enable lineage tracking
• Industry standard metadata — widely preserved in professional workflows
limitations:
• XMP metadata can be stripped by social media and messaging apps
• AI tools may not embed XMP metadata at all
• Edit history can be manually fabricated using metadata editors
• Consumer cameras often don't write XMP data
• Complex edit histories may be inconclusive
